chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, with an unbroken chain, said:

Whenever Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) recited this Verse: 'And if you would count Allah's favours, you will not be able to number them', he would say: 'Glory be to the One Who never Made it to be in anyone the recognition of His Favours except for the recognition falling short of (Al-Taqseer) recognising, just as He has never Made it to be in anyone the recognition of being aware of Him more than the knowledge that He cannot be perceived.'

So gratitude be to the Majestic and Mighty for the recognition of the recognisers by their reduced recognition as appreciation, so He Made their reduced recognition as an expression of gratitude, just as He Knows that the knowledge of the knowledgeable people would not be able to perceived Him, so He made Belief as knowledge from it, so they cannot exceed that.

So no one from His creatures can reach the limit of worshipping Him, and how can one reach the limit of worship of the One Who has no Limits for Him, impossible! Allah is Higher than that, Exalted and Great.

key_terms.التَّقْصِير: Shortcoming or falling short; the inherent limitation in human capacity to fully recognize or count divine favors.
key_terms.عُلُوّاً كَبِيراً: Great elevation; describing God's transcendence above human limits.
key_terms.مَدَى: Limit or extent; referring to the boundless nature of God's worship and essence.
key_terms.مَعْرِفَةُ إِدْرَاكِهِ: The recognition of His perception/essence; the cognitive grasp of God by creation.

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali explain the relationship between human limitation and gratitude for God's infinite favors?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) elucidates the theological paradox that human inability to fully enumerate or comprehend God's blessings is not a deficiency, but rather the very essence of gratitude (*shukr*). This perspective aligns with Shia gnosis, where recognizing the limits of human capacity to grasp the Divine is itself an act of worship, as God’s essence transcends all finite measurement. The Imam thus redefines 'shortcoming' not as failure, but as the appropriate epistemological stance before the Infinite.

en.sarwar: 593. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al-Husayn, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hisham, from Anbasat Bin Bajaad Al-Abid, from Jabir, who has said: ‘We were in the presence Abu Ja’far (a.s.), and the authority of the Clan of Umayya was mentioned, so Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said: ‘No one comes out (rebels) against Hisham except that he gets killed’. ‘And he (a.s.) also mentioned that his government would last for twenty years’. He (the narrator) said, ‘That grieved us’.

So he (a.s.) said: ‘What is the matter with you? Whenever Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic Intends to Destroy the authority of a people, He (azwj) Commands the Angel to quicken the pace of the orbit in accordance to what He (azwj) Intends to’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So we said to Zayd, ‘This is the discussion we had’.

So he said, ‘I witnessed Hisham, and the Rasool Allah (saww) was insulted in his presence, so he neither denied that, nor did he change it. By Allah (azwj)! Even if there is no one except for myself and my son, I would come out (in rebellion) against him’.
